title: the compiler-recognized Context.context member cannot be detached from its capability and invoked reflectively; the detachment itself is refused
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Context Access': '`Capability.context()` MUST be an inherited, compiler-recognized call on subclasses of `Context`.' A call is recognized at the CALL; `Reader.context` alone is a value, and once it is a value the recognizer has nothing left to see. `Reflect.apply` then invokes it with `Reader` as the receiver, so the read really happens — this is not a hypothetical laundering route. On the pre-fix tree this exact program was accepted by BOTH backends with `requirements: []`, and the reference lane RAN it: it printed the capability's value out of a function whose certified row named nothing. That makes this the worst member of the detached family and the reason it is the one written as a case. The refusal is reported at the detachment (column 25 is `Reader.context`, the member selection), not at the `Reflect.apply` call, because the rule is about the member reference and not about which host function consumes it — an implementation that keyed on `Reflect.apply` would leave `.call`, `.bind`, an alias, a destructuring and a template interpolation open, and the sibling case `a-bound-context-reference-is-rejected` exists to hold the second of those. PIN THE SMITHERS CODE, NOT THE TYPESCRIPT ONE: before 2026-08-26 the reference refused several members of this family INCIDENTALLY, with `TS2571` out of the prelude's typing of a detached receiver, while the fork's looser prelude typing accepted them outright — a verdict divergence resting on a typing accident rather than on a rule. Both backends now answer `SMITHERS2107` alone here, because a frontend refusal short-circuits the emitted-TypeScript stage under the default `noEmitOnError`, so the TS code is gone from the observation on both sides. Declaring it would have re-pinned the accident. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the message (SMITHERS2107 carries a fixed sentence with no payload), and the enumeration's completeness — `Reflect.get(Reader, computedKey)` with a non-literal key is a recorded open residual on both backends, and pretending otherwise by writing a case that passes for the wrong reason would be worse than recording it. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared column from 25 to 26 turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 60e661fa93b5c89246fe582c4cfaab9dbcf81e0f6e330ded4a7c080195c2edec before and after). The paired positive control is `a-member-named-context-on-an-ordinary-value-stays-ordinary`, which detaches a member spelled `context` from a plain object and from an ordinary class, reads one through `Reflect.get`, and names `typeof Reader.context` in a TYPE position — all of which must keep compiling and RUNNING, so a rule that keys on the member's NAME rather than on its resolved symbol turns that case red.
